x: We have the talent, some of it already shown, some of it dormant, but to mention only these few names is to comment on a strength which could do much: Broadbent, Botwright, Burfitt, Blowfield, Nankeville, Marchant, Herbert, Read, Lucas, Stimpson.

Dick Tobin lead the field out at a fair pace, then bunched together were Carter, Bill Lucas, Clinton, Abberton, Eales, Blowfield, Penny, with Footer and Morrell a little behind, and Len Herbert at the rear.
At the halfway stage Arthur Penny and Vic Blowfield were running together with the rest of the field strung out in this order—Pearson, Frost, Eales, Tobin, Stokell.
The placings in our club five miles were repeated with Vic Blowfield once again leading the field home. Scoring six aside the team result was: Belgrave H. 28 points, Oxford University 50 points.

Ted Stimpson was always well up with the first dozen runners, but Vern Blowfield was suffering with shoe trouble and was gradually dropping back while Len Herbert and Marchant were striving to hold their places, but things did not look too good for our prospects of retaining our title as Southern champions.

Our team got away to a good start and quickly showed to advantage with Derrick Burfitt and Vern Blowfield among the leaders. Derrick and Olney (T.V.H.) soon sorted themselves out and together fighting all the way Olney eventually won on the tape by taking the "proverbial deep breath," the timekeeper…
At the half-distance Vic Blowfield and Frank Abberton were together in the lead with Bill Lucas and Len Marchant fairly handy, but the rest of the field were already well strung out.
Bishop (winner's time, 1 min. 57.8 secs.) 1 mile: 1st, Marchant; 2nd, Bromley. 4 min. 26 secs. 2 miles: 1st, Blowfield, 9 min. 41 secs.; 2nd.

On the 19th November we had Woodford Green A.C. and the Royal Military Police (Woking) as visitors to Belgrave Hall, for an 8 aside match over our 5 miles cross-country course. Bromley of the Police was first man home just in front of Vern Blowfield and Jack Brown.
Vern Blowfield had an easy run in fourth position and it looks as if these three will form the spearhead of our team for the coming cross-country championships.

At the half-distance there was a group of four runners with Brown, Blowfield, Bill Lucas and Steve Charlton all nicely together in under the half-hour, which is good running for our five miles course.
Vern Blowfield was our next runner, and behind him were Woodford Green, Essex Beagles and Aylesford, battling together, and the latter two clubs were represented by J.

The other members finished as follows:—Charlton 16th, Tobin 33rd, Ken Stimpson 45th, MacDonald 59th, Heard 68th and Housego 127th. The team finished fifth, quite a good performance without such stars as Burfitt, Blowfield and Smart.

Blowfield and Jack Brown were now in the thirties with Walker and Eddie Short also inside the fifty's, but our last two scoring men were still much too far back to stand a chance of securing a place in the team race.
